For 2 years I waited for this game and finally, finally I can see it with my own eyes. Dying Light 2 is gorgeous to look at. The sunset, the volumetric fog and lighting, the green and vibrant rooftops where humanity is thriving (even growing vegetables). And all these contrasted with a decaying filth filled street level straight of Fallout 4. The story and characters are great when compared to Dying Light. The soundtrack, okayish

I saw a lot of people hate on this game but i mostly think its cause people were blinded from the first game nostalgia the parkour in this game is amazing and i liked it more then the first game parkour, the combat also have pretty cool mechanics that the first game didnt have i really liked the faction system where you can choose regions for a faction and the region changes depending on the faction governs it, the Visuals in my opinion were pretty sick both old villedor and new villedor were unique in they're own way i enjoyed the old style of building of old villedor and i enjoyed the modern buildings and towers of new villedor i saw some people hate on the feature of needing UV source all the time or you will die in dark zones after a period of time but honestly it makes sense in the first game people relied on antizin to not turn and in dying light 2 theres no antizin anymore so they rely on UV sources to delay their infection but it doesnt stop it, the story was also pretty great in my opinion your choices can change a lot of events in the story which made it more interesting and the ending was pretty sick and sad in the same time and overall this game is too hated.

most broken game I have ever played. story sucks, parkour is buggy, have to setup controls and graphics every startup, some safe zones wont activate, choices in the game don't really matter, story is very predictable, enemies are easy even on the hardest difficulty, loot sucks, enemies are basically all the same with very slight differences (they are all like the first game with only two exceptions i believe) one brawler challenge will force your game to close, immersion is often ruined, voice acting sounds like they picked up a dude from mcdonalds and asked them to read a line (probably asked them to write the story too), enemies often randomly die, Character heads often spin on their bodies, all the new skills are bugged (some has been fixed) graphics are fantastic even without ray-tracing. highly recommend if you get it at half price. got much more but i honestly hope they fix all this. parkour is still awesome though. Too bad the combat is as bland as black desert grinding. I hope you enjoy this game however I have been unable to and wouldnt recommend it to anyone in its current state.

For me, one of the core pillars of a good zombie game is combat as majority of your time spent is in combat. The first Dying Light had VERY good/fun combat physics. Right when I started the game I could tell the physics were not on the same level as the first. Combat did not feel fun and dynamic like the first, but felt rather repetitive and boring. The combat bothered me the most of many flaws I noticed. I'd watch some gameplay, a review, or a comparison between the first and second game before buying this. I really wanted to like this game and even bought it at release, but in the end all I wanted was a refund.

If you loved the first Dying Light, I'd be very cautious about buying this game.

Tırmanması hoplaması ve dünyası çok güzel. Fakat combat sistemi rezalet ve oyundan soğumama yol açtığından böyle bırakacağım

1.Gece vakti Volatile zombilerini, gta'nın yıldız-polis sisteminin daha boktanlısına dönüştürmüşler. Bir volatile sizi görürse, 2 (+sınırsız) tane daha direkt ayağınızın dibinde yok yerden kapak açılıp ortaya çıkıyor. Asla yeneyim de devam edeyim yok. Herhangi bir başarı duygusu yok.

2.Zombilere tükürük eklemişler, keskin nişancı mübarek. Baktı AI'sı patlıyor ulaşamıyor sana, uzaktan tükürüp 100 100 vurmaya başlıyor, ulan ben silah buldum, yay buldum, arbalet buldum. o kadar vurmuyor amk... Bir de insan utanır ıskalar falan, yok!

3. Düzgün yan görevler eğlenceli çünkü dünyası güzel ve keşfetmek için teşvik ediyor. Fakat Challange'lar için zaten ayrı bir sekme varken, kalabalık olsun diye yan görevler sekmesine de neden ucuzca koydunuz anlamadım. Görev alıcam, npc ile konuşuyorum, adam bana parkur challenge'ını bitir görevi koyuyor. Utanmanız yok mu oğlum? Zaten aşırı sıkıcı hepsi.

Şu oyunu tam seveceğim. Herhangi bir gece görevi, combat sekansı çıkınca bayıyorum. Bu kadar mükemmel bir formül hazırlayıp, nasıl batırdınız, veya da nasıl çözmemekte ısrar ediyorsunuz ilginç cidden. Umarım yeni oyunda düzeltirsiniz. 1'de gece korkutucu veya zorlayıcı olabiliyordu. 2'de bunlardan daha çok sinir bozucu ve soğutucu olmuş.

This game was very fun to play. Although there were many bugs in the game but it was a pleasant experience in the open world. Almost all the time I got sucked into the world, killing zombies, roaming around and completing side quests. I got sucked in so hard that I played 100+ hours within 2 weeks which is very rare for me. I've heard the story was mediocre from others but I found it not that bad. Yes the story kinda doesn't make you care about anyone but I can look the other way this time because the game was good. Overall I'd recommend this game if you love to roam around and do stuff instead of focusing hard on the story which isn't half bad

Parkour feels clunky, oftentimes the character doesn't do what you told him to do, slow-mos turn multiplayer into an utterly confusing teleportation simulator and since everyone's an archer (balance) there's a ton of those in each fight. It wasn’t bad, but it wasn’t good either. Here’s why, Dying Light 1 was super fun. The movement and upgrade system for combat and parkour made you actually feel stronger and faster as you leveled up, and the grapple aspect was amazing.

With this game, it just felt flat. I only wanted to play the story and skip the side quests because upgrading parkour perks and combat perks felt pretty useless. The grapple and flying? Honestly sucked, slow and clunky compared to the first game. The pacing was super slow too, and it never really gave me that Dying Light 1 feeling.

The ending dragged on, and I actually dropped the game after a few days, only coming back to finish it because the new game was about to drop. I’m really hoping the next one captures the magic of the first.

This has been bitter-sweet for me. The sweet part is that it's a fun game with a lot of content, the campaign mode is nice and long plus the story is enjoyable. There's plenty of loot to collect and weapons to upgrade in all the usual ways for this series.

Most of the neat combat and parkour abilities are back with a few new ones to try out. Useful tools to help speed up travel, which changes quite a bit when you switch between areas. The larger area will have you change up how you get about going around town.

The bitter part comes from a massive pile of bugs to wade through. Little things from flickering or transparent textures to big things like having to restart your game whenever a quest doesn't want to process.

It seems quite a bit buggier when playing co-op, setting it to solo seems to reduce the bugs a little. On that note I had to wait a little over a month to be able to play with my friends because of a friends list bug that would have required me to delete 700 friends just to play.

It's playable and there's plenty to enjoy so I'm not saying the game is bad but it definitely needs a bit more work!

You know, i was really excited for this game. but it just doesn't have it. i know exhilarating feedback and total constructive criticism but it feels like a shadow of the first game. and it was disappointing. i unfortunately didn't even finish it so maybe it gets better.

really fun game, but false advertisement. the developers kept bragging about how there is hundreds of hours worth of gameplay in this game. not only did i do every easter egg, and do every side quest, but i also did the entire main quest and got all of my stats up to max, and as you can see i didnt even hit 100 hours. and some of that time i was just exploring and just playing with friends and helping them with missions. maybe a total of 50 to 60 hours total. which is still alot, but just way too exaggerated. all in all still a great game and it was really fun to play. but like i said, dont be expecting hundreds of hours worth of gameplay.

I finished the game, so that's something. But there was a lot of hate involved in playing, and more so towards the end. The ending was lame, with boring fights and dumb fail states from a bygone era of game design.

The mid-game is fun: free-running through the city and having enough power to take on baddies without being overpowered. That's when the game is actually good.

If I could go back, I would refund the game before the two-hour mark.
But if you need an open-world game to listen to podcasts, this might be okay if it's on sale.
Also: Fuck Aiden; he's such a lame, whiny main character. His voice acting was painful to listen to.

I thought Dying Light 2 was getting better and for a time, it was even though it had a rocky start.

Then Techland got bought out by Tencent. Now it has micro-transactions, for a PvE single-player/co-op game that costs $60 on average,

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3032355959

This is just another slap to the face after seeing how much DL2 got downgraded, most of the promises shown early were never fulfilled, and the "Bloody Ties" DLC was subpar. I'll probably still keep playing this game because a good friend of mine gifted it for my birthday but otherwise, I strongly recommend to stay away from DL2 and anything related to Tencent.

It's clear where the direction of this game is headed and it's sad.
Micro transactions for a mainly singleplayer game. You can’t even see what you buy in-game!! I’m just so sad. Was a huge fan….

I think the parkour is more fun than the last game. Its smooth and it was satisfying going from roof to roof. 

The combat is good at humans this time and it was repetitive on zombies compare to 1 where its the 
opposite. 

The story is okay... With the way they advertised the game as the "where your choices could change everything" it felt like all of the choices I've made still ends up on the same outcome-- except when you have to assign which faction controls the structures and stuff.

I liked some of the characters like Jai, Sophie, Frank and Juan but as you progress to the story, you just don't see them ever again. 

The night time isn't as scary as before but i still liked it. It was very arcade-y. 

The game's so fun and it could be so good if not for the bugs and glitches that i encounter every time i boot up the game.

Last night I tried playing with good headphones and a dark room. This game is terrifyingly awesome.
The sound is amazing. I was missing so much hi-deff sound before. Its like a whole new game with some good head phones , holy crap.

Compared to Dying Light 1, the game only got worse. The story is so flawed and stupid, mechanics are just as wonky as before and all the new things make the game just easier and more repetetive. Absolutely do not buy.

Good game but its missing a Death Cam
A good designer on the dl2 team, Antonio G. is a specialist for this, hopefully techy will put him on it asap

Newer weapon and outfit bundles use points instead of just being normal Steam DLC. And of course, you can never buy the exact amount of points you need, you always have some left over. Additionally, some items are time-limited like the "Let It Snow Weapon Pack" and "Mischievous Helper Bundle" at the time of this review. A definite step down compared to how the first game did DLC.
Monotonous gameplay, story that really wants you to get emotionally invested but didn't do anything for me. Dropkicking everyone was fun though.
Really good open world zombie game with great parkour and story hopefully we get the same energy for the next dying light game!

The millionth part of the first game
I admire you Techland, you took everything you learned in DL1 (an almost perfect game btw), and sent it all to hell.
It really has the potential to be these days what DL1 was in its generation, but was it really necessary to add those super invasive RPG elements? Decisions that don't affect the story at all, a map in which you are not totally free, super flat dialogues and characters, NO variety of quests .
It hurts me a lot because I love the saga, but that's as far as my ride in Villedor goes.
Good graphics and mapping by the way, too bad they are overshadowed by all the negative aspects of the game.

The second Dying Light game, finished it late after relese, was good? I would say yes, this game it's not meant to be a next of DL1, it's made to be a different experience, something new, and for me it succed. The story keeps me courios till the end, and also there exists choices that are leading you to one of a few endings, idk if it's two or more, doesn't matter, the game wins the Dying Light name and it's totally worth to try.

I've played the first game at least 5 times beginning through end, max levelling my character and exploring every nook and cranny of the map. I beat all DLCs including The Following twice, so needless to say I was super hyped when DL2 was announced. Unfortunately, this game is by far worse than the original one. The story is uninteresting so far, the characters forgettable, the parkour floaty, the gameplay buggy and unsatisfying and it feels like there's basically no progression. In the first game I was a government agent dropped into a zone of mutants and infected, slowly uncovering the world and improving my survival skills. In this one, I'm already an established person (or so you would think) but apparently I don't know how to do just about any basic thing. Awfully convenient writing/game logic but extremely unsatisfying way to create an arc for your main character and story. I think I'll just stick to the memories made in the original game, had a ton of fun there and played literally every single piece of content that I could (except Hellraid, lol)

LET ME START OFF BY SAYING THAT WHEN I FIRST PLAYED DYING LIGHT 2 WHEN IT CAME OUT (and before this latest update), I ACTUALLY LOVED IT. I thought it was an excellent addition to the Dying Light Universe, and there was so much hype when this game came out back in 2022.

Now trying to jump back into this game four years later (I still haven't beat this, by the way) and Techland decided to give this game the worst possible update ever. I'll admit that I wasn't a big fan of the prologue because of how long it was, but now that it's gone, it's completely ruined the game for me. Why would you remove something that most of the fanbase loved? Not to mention removing the prologue completely cuts a bunch of context from the game that is VERY MUCH NEEDED, MIND YOU. 

Do yourself a HUGE favor and buy the first game, STAY AWAY from this second game, and MAYBE consider DL: THE BEAST at a considerable discount. Or if you intend to play this game anyway, at least look up an old playthrough of the older versions of the game to get the proper context since Techland is apparently a bunch of idiots.

People crap on this game. It IS a good game. The city scape is NOT as good as is in the original. But everything else is honestly an upgrade. With one other exception. In this game zombies at night are not scary. Eventually you can make your character strong enough to just shit on them. Very playable, very fun in 2026. Though i heard at release it was a bugged mess, it is now fixed.

reason.text: Negative reviews from this period mostly object to microtransactions added to a full-priced single-player game, with some tying this to the Tencent buyout.
A news headline from the same month covers microtransactions sparking review bombing, and an official announcement changed mod-related EULA terms.

lines.F1: Dying Light 2 Stay Human: Reloaded Edition had a negative surge (far more negative reviews than usual, often called a review bomb), Sep 2023
lines.F2: Sep 2023: 41% positive across 1,532 reviews (905 negative), against a usual 76% positive and 237 negative a month
lines.R4: (negative review, 43h played) "STAY AWAY. Microtransactions in a full priced game. Broken promises and lost potential. Pay to win garbage. Lackluster updates. Techland hate their customers and love nothing more than draining every penny out of you that they can."
lines.R5: (negative review, 100h played) "DO NOT BUY THIS GAME Techland was just bought out by Tencent and almost immediately started rolling out a microtransaction system to their already subpar game. Even worse, they've pretty much said that any modding is not allowed and reserve the..."
lines.R6: (negative review, 30h played) "Imagine selling yourself to a predatory company, adding micro transactions to mostly a single-player game, that mostly has quite low player numbers. It's a real shame. Not to mention predatory scam pricing."
lines.R10: (negative review, 545h played) "I thought Dying Light 2 was getting better and for a time, it was even though it had a rocky start. Then Techland got bought out by Tencent. Now it has micro-transactions, for a PvE single-player/co-op game that costs $60 on average,..."
lines.R14: (negative review, 253h played) "I cant recommend this game as techland introduced a predatory in-game shop and in-game currency such as the one found in Fortine and various browser based free-to-play games. I'll change my review if they do away with it"
lines.N4: 2023-09-11, PCGamesN: Dying Light 2 microtransactions spark review bombing, Techland replies

news.title: Dying Light 2 microtransactions spark review bombing, Techland replies

tldr.text: Mostly Positive (77%) overall, but recent reviews are less positive than the all-time score.
Players love the story and combat, but many find the characters weak and report bugs and crashes.

details.text: Recent reviews complain less about bugs and crashes, but more about music and sound, with one calling it "charging $20 for ai audio".
Players who reviewed with under 2 hours logged are far less positive, at 47%, than those who played longer.
